thesis: Vontier reported Q3 2026 on Nov 5 (8-K). Core sales grew 5.7% and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.92, ahead of its own guidance on sales, margin and EPS; the full-year adjusted EPS outlook was raised to $3.60-3.64 and Q4 guidance set at $0.99-1.03. The company also repurchased $280M of stock year to date. The shares gapped up from $37.58 at the Nov 5 open and rose another ~5.8% to $42.23 today on 3.1x volume. Counter-evidence named and not fully resolved: reported sales fell 2.1% because of the Teletrac Navman divestiture, the Q4 guide implies core growth slowing to about 3%, and Repair Solutions is under macro pressure on technicians' discretionary spending. Litigation and governance checks found only ordinary-course matters and older law-firm solicitations, with no restatement or charges. A confirmed, company-specific beat-and-raise with an unresolved growth-deceleration counter-case puts this at medium.
invalidation: Q4 core growth comes in below the ~3% guide or Repair Solutions weakness spreads, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$37.58).
sources: Business Wire (2024 law-firm solicitation, no finding): https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240917895681/en

thesis: Fox Corporation completed its acquisition of Roku on Nov 6, well ahead of the 2027 target, after the Justice Department closed its antitrust review. Roku holders receive $95.30 in cash plus 0.9799 Fox Class A shares per share, and Roku's listing ends with the closing. Today's 4.4x volume at a near-flat $160.54 is mechanical deal-close trading tied to that consideration, not an independent fundamental signal. Litigation checks found merger-related law-firm solicitations and a Delaware Chancery putative class action filed by a Fox stockholder, with no scheduled ruling found. There is no standalone equity left to own, so this is low; avoid.
invalidation: Not applicable: the shares are converting into the merger consideration.

thesis: Five9 reported Q3 2026 on Nov 5. Revenue rose 13% to $323.3M and adjusted EPS of $0.82 beat by about $0.02, but Q4 adjusted EPS guidance of $0.88-0.92 sits well below the ~$0.99 consensus, full-year adjusted EPS was cut to $3.17-3.21 from $3.22-3.30, and adjusted gross margin slipped to 61.7% from 62.8%. It also agreed to buy Level AI for $325M in cash, excluded from guidance. Evercore downgraded the shares to In-Line, and they fell about 17.7% to $28.11 on 4.1x volume. The strongest counter-case is the CEO's AI momentum and the Q3 beat, but a guidance cut and margin slippage outweigh it on the company's own outlook. A 2024-vintage securities class action reportedly survived a motion to dismiss, with no scheduled ruling found. This run found no primary or wire source for the guidance figures, which caps this at medium; avoid.
invalidation: Q4 results beat the cut guidance and margins recover, or Level AI shows a clear early revenue contribution.

thesis: OUTFRONT reported Q3 2026 after the Nov 5 close (8-K). Revenue rose 9.3% to $511.1M and adjusted OIBDA rose 5.9% to $145.3M, but SG&A grew 23.1%, partly from a higher bad debt allowance, and operating expenses rose 5.3% on higher MTA guaranteed payments. The shares fell about 3.8% to $30.79 on 3.8x volume, and this run found no coverage explaining the reaction or any guidance change. Litigation checks found only routine, non-material matters in the 10-Qs. Revenue growth offset by faster cost growth leaves the read mixed, so this is low; avoid.
invalidation: Cost growth moderates and the revenue gains convert into faster OIBDA and AFFO growth.

thesis: Lionsgate Studios reported fiscal Q2 2027 after the Nov 5 close (8-K). Revenue rose 41% to $668.8M, operating income swung to $29.1M from a $46.0M loss, adjusted OIBDA rose to $72.0M from $14.1M, and trailing 12-month library revenue reached $1.04B. Management reaffirmed its forecast of significant adjusted OIBDA growth this year. The shares rose about 13.2% to $14.22 on 3.7x volume. Counter-evidence named and not fully resolved: there is still a GAAP net loss of $15.5M, shareholders' equity is negative, and the quarter leaned on one film (Michael). Litigation checks found a noteholder suit over a 2024 indenture amendment in discovery, with no scheduled ruling, and an SEC comment-letter exchange on the FY2026 10-K with no restatement disclosed; neither meets a risk_flags criterion. A confirmed, company-specific beat with these open balance-sheet and concentration counter-cases puts this at medium.
invalidation: Adjusted OIBDA growth stalls in the back half or the balance sheet weakens further, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$12.56).

thesis: JFrog reported Q3 2026 on Nov 5 (8-K). Revenue grew 31% to $179.2M, cloud revenue grew 60% to $101.5M, trailing net dollar retention rose to 124% from 118%, the non-GAAP operating margin was 22.7%, and free cash flow was $66.5M. It guided Q4 revenue to $183-185M and full-year 2026 revenue to $680-682M. The shares jumped about 35.3% to $100.99 on 3.6x volume. Counter-evidence named and not fully resolved: GAAP operating income is still slightly negative, share-based compensation was $41.8M in the quarter, and the Q4 guide implies only about 2-3% sequential growth; this run could not confirm the size of any full-year raise against prior guidance. An aggregator article claiming a revenue restatement cites no filing or docket, and EDGAR shows no amended 10-K, so it does not meet the governance_history criterion. A confirmed, company-specific beat with an open growth-durability counter-case puts this at medium.
invalidation: Cloud growth or net dollar retention decelerates materially, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$74.62).
sources: SEC EDGAR (10-K filing list, no amendments shown): https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001800667&type=10-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=40

thesis: Rhythm rose about 6.9% to $112.22 on 3.4x volume. This run found Wall Street Journal and Reuters reports that AstraZeneca made a non-binding offer of roughly $10B (about $124 a share, up to $134 with milestones) through Alexion. Neither company has confirmed it, and this run could not tie those reports' timing to today's move. The litigation and governance check found no lawsuit, investigation or restatement; its results covered only the earlier FDA review extension for IMCIVREE in acquired hypothalamic obesity, and they did not show that application's outcome. A move resting on an unconfirmed report leaves the evidence unresolved, so this is low; avoid.
invalidation: A bid or deal is confirmed by the company, or company-disclosed fundamentals explain the move.

thesis: Extreme Networks jumped about 14.1% to $24.02 on 3.2x volume after a Nov 6 Reuters report, citing sources, that it is working with an investment bank on a possible sale following buyer approaches; Fortinet, Cisco and NetApp were named as potential suitors. The company declined to comment, and no transaction is certain. Underneath that, the Oct 28 fiscal Q1 2027 report (8-K) was confirmed and company-specific: revenue grew 10% to $341.1M, SaaS ARR grew 22%, and full-year guidance was raised to $1.402-1.412B in revenue and $1.35-1.39 non-GAAP EPS. Counter-evidence named and not resolved: much of today's gain rests on an unconfirmed, still-pending sale process that may not happen. A securities class action over 2022-2024 statements is proceeding after a motion to dismiss was denied, with no scheduled ruling found. With a real fundamental catalyst but a pending, unconfirmed deal driving the move, this is medium.
invalidation: The sale process ends without a deal and the growth guidance slips, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$21.05).

thesis: Janus Living rose about 4.0% to $31.99 on 3.0x volume. This run found that it priced an upsized offering of 26.25M Class A-1 shares at $28.50, with a ~3.9M-share underwriter option, expected to close Nov 6, alongside a Q3 revenue beat and a raised 2026 adjusted FFO outlook. The new issuance meets the dilution_risk criterion. Its own filings describe it as a Healthpeak-controlled company without independent compensation or nominating committees, with related-party agreements not negotiated at arm's length. No specific lawsuit or investigation was found. Dilution plus the controlled-company conflicts make this low; avoid.
invalidation: Issuance stops, Healthpeak's control and conflict structure is reduced, and operating growth carries through.
sources: SEC S-11 (controlled company, conflicts of interest): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002100805/000110465926122669/tmb-20260930xs11.htm

thesis: Fox completed its roughly $22B acquisition of Roku on Nov 6, paying $95.30 in cash plus 0.9799 Fox Class A shares per Roku share. Former Roku holders now own about 26% of Fox, a completed share issuance that meets the dilution_risk criterion. The company targets about $400M of run-rate cost synergies within two years. FOXA slipped about 1.5% to $66.64 on 3.6x volume, which reads as mechanical deal-close and index-rebalancing flow rather than a new fundamental signal. Litigation checks found a Delaware Chancery putative class action by a Fox stockholder (filed Aug 28) and merger law-firm solicitations, with no scheduled ruling found. Dilution and a mechanical move make this low; avoid.
invalidation: Integration delivers the synergy target and the combined business grows earnings per share despite the larger share count.

thesis: Guardant Health reported Q3 2026 on Nov 5 (8-K). Revenue grew 36% to $361.0M, screening revenue grew 180% on about 83,000 Shield tests, and oncology grew 25%. 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $1.36-1.37B from $1.34-1.36B, and the Shield volume guide to 285,000-290,000. The shares eased about 1.2% to $151.53 on 2.9x volume. Counter-evidence named and not resolved: the net loss widened to $124.4M and the full-year free-cash-flow burn guide was widened to $205-220M from $195-205M. The 10-Q discloses an April 2026 False Claims Act civil investigative demand on federal billing, which is open-ended with no scheduled step, and Natera is appealing Guardant's $287M false-advertising judgment to the Ninth Circuit; neither meets a risk_flags criterion. A confirmed raise against a widening cash burn puts this at medium.
invalidation: Shield volume growth or the revenue raise falters, cash burn widens again, or the False Claims Act matter escalates.

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 22). ROIV rose about 6.3% to $38.94 on 1.7x volume, and this run's search found no new company disclosure explaining it. It remains above the ~$34.92 pre-announcement level. The thesis rests on the Oct 21 CLARITY Phase 3 results: brepocitinib met the primary and all key secondary endpoints in non-infectious uveitis, and it carries Breakthrough Therapy Designation. The counter-case named in the prior thesis remains open: the uveitis indication is not yet approved, and the sNDA is not planned until 1H 2027. Fiscal Q2 results on Nov 9 are an unresolved scheduled event before the next review. The search found the 2026 Moderna patent settlement and continuing litigation against Pfizer and BioNTech, with no scheduled ruling found. This stays medium.
invalidation: Full CLARITY data, Nov 9 results or FDA feedback reveal a safety or efficacy problem, or a close back below the pre-announcement level (~$34.92).

thesis: Held position (opened Oct 28 on the Oct 27 proposal). It remains above the ~$68.03 pre-report level. The thesis rests on the company-specific Oct 27 Q3 report: EPS of $0.58 against a $0.07 consensus. Centene class action with no scheduled ruling. These cap this at medium.
invalidation: Medicaid cost trends worsen enough to put the raised guidance at risk, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$68.03).

thesis: Held position (opened Nov 3 on the Nov 2 proposal). NWL was flat at $5.48, below the $5.82 entry, and this run's search found no new company disclosure. It remains above the ~$5.08 pre-report invalidation level. The litigation check found an April 2026 CrockPot multicooker product-liability suit with no scheduled ruling, and older 2018-2020 securities matters. The counter-cases named in the prior thesis remain open and keep the evidence mixed: the Oct 30 Q3 report cut the operating cash flow outlook about 62% to $150M, cited about $220M of inflation headwinds and a $101M impairment, and only maintained full-year adjusted EPS guidance, against 3.7% sales growth and a 90bp normalized margin gain. The early-exit guard applies (the opening buy was 3 trading days ago), and there is no new fact, so the direction stays long. This stays low, and the stop-loss and conviction-trim still protect the position.
invalidation: Q4 results miss the $0.17-0.19 EPS guide or the cash-flow outlook is cut again, a further impairment, or a close back below the pre-report level (~$5.08).
